title: Fenix Claims inference economics workbench
content:
Purpose and context:
This is a working workbook for the Fenix (claims processing) pilot — a before/after cost and ops analysis applying Redwood Optimize recommendations. Goal: quantify realistic token/unit savings, list recommended runway changes, and draft a lightweight ops runbook for rollout (canary -> full).

Status: rough numbers derived from a 7-day sample (2026-02-01 to 2026-02-07) provided by Fenix engineering. Numbers are noisy; next step is a second 14-day pull with percentile gating.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Baseline (current stack): mixture of 7B open model + custom reranking service. Avg throughput 180 reqs/min; median decode latency 420ms; estimated infra cost ~$3,400/day (tokens + infra) for production traffic profile.
- Redwood Optimize proposal (conservative incremental changes): apply dynamic batching + KV prefix caching + switch to 4-bit quantized model variant for retrieval-heavy paths. Estimated infra cost ~$1,920/day. Net savings: ~43% ($1,480/day).
- Faster scenario (aggressive): add live rerouting to cheaper region + model distillation for short-form responses => projected savings up to 58% ($1,972/day) but with higher QA/regression risk.

Baseline metrics (7-day sample):
| metric | value | notes |
| tokens/day | 28,400,000 | includes prompts + responses (est) |
| avg req size (tokens) | 215 | skewed by long claim narratives |
| median latency | 420ms | end-to-end decode (includes reranker) |
| infra spend/day | $2,400 | GPU + node services (billing sample) |
| model costs/day | $1,000 | third-party model licensing + per-token estimate |
| total cost/day | $3,400 | baseline used for comparisons |

Assumptions used in projections (call these out):
- Quantization efficacy: 4-bit quant reduces GPU token cost by ~36% while increasing inference time by ~5-12% for long sequences; we assume 8% latency hit in conservative calc.
- KV prefix cache hit rate: expected 28% on claim templates and boilerplate (pilot logs show ~22% in sample; we use 28% as achievable with small prompt normalization).
- Batching improvements: continuous batching at 50–120ms windows, effective throughput improves by 22% on CPU/GPU util.
- Routing fallbacks: 10% of requests may route to a higher-capacity model at peak; fallback cost accounted for in sensitivity table.

Redwood Optimize proposal (conservative bundle):
1) Prompt normalization + lightweight hashing to improve KV cache hits (~+6pp)
2) Enable continuous batching with adaptive window (target: 70ms)
3) Deploy 4-bit quantized variant for non-sensitive inference paths (retrieval + template responses)
4) Configure policy-based routing: user-tiered fallback, prefer cheaper region for non-US requests
Estimated impact (conservative):
- tokens/day: ~27,800,000 (slight drop due to prompt cleanup)
- infra spend/day: $1,380
- model costs/day: $540
- total cost/day: $1,920
- savings vs baseline: $1,480/day (~43%)

Sensitivity analysis (quick):
- Low improvement case (KV 18% hit, quantization results worse): savings ~22% ($748/day)
- High improvement case (KV 40% hit, distillation + routing): savings ~58% ($1,972/day)

Breakdown by recommended action (estimated):
- KV caching (+prompt normalization): saves $520/day (35% of total savings)
- Continuous batching config: saves $410/day (28%)
- Quantized model variant: saves $360/day (24%)
- Routing to cheaper region: saves $190/day (13%)

Operational considerations / risks:
- Quality regression: quantized outputs must be validated against the critical claim-handling prompts. Need 200 prompt-level evals and 5k token-sampled checks before full rollout.
- Cold-starts and cache warming: expect 18–36 hours for cache to reach steady-state on production traffic; schedule canary during low-volume window.
- Compliance: certain PII-heavy paths cannot use offsite cheaper regions; flagged list needed.
- Observability: must add per-route token-level costing and alert for >15% immediate delta after rollout.

Mini runbook (canary -> full):
- Step 0: branch/infra prep: create quantized model variant image + config toggles for batching/cache/routing (PRs linked).
- Step 1: internal QA: run automated eval suite (200 critical prompts) and manual spot-check (5 reviewers) -> signoff.
- Step 2: Canary (1% traffic, 6 hours): monitor latency, error rate, quality score via eval harness.
- Step 3: Ramp (1% -> 25% over 24h): watch cost delta, cache-hit %, tail latencies.
- Step 4: Full (25% -> 100% over 48–72h) if steady.
- Rollback criteria: >5% absolute drop in key-quality metric OR >15% increase in median tail latency OR >10% higher cost than expected for 2 consecutive hours.

Open items / TODOs:
- [ ] Confirm region eligibility for PII against Fenix legal (ticket: JIRA-SEC-839).
- [ ] Get final 14-day sample from Fenix infra team (Marcus to own).
- [ ] Prepare 200-prompt eval set and schedule manual review (Aditi to coordinate).
- [ ] Add per-route token cost dashboard (dash id: dashboard/opt-fenix-07).

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Need to double-check the licensing delta if Fenix moves to a customer-hosted model (cost math changes).
- PR #27 in github contains the quant-variant build; runtime perf is slightly better than the build logs.

Appendix: quick math examples
- If KV hit increases from 22% -> 30%: token throughput saved = 28,400,000 * 0.08 = 2,272,000 tokens/day -> value @ $0.00012/token = $272/day saved (example).
- Continuous batching improvement: 22% throughput gain approximated by reducing effective per-token GPU-ms. Translate to infra spend reduction using current baseline utilization.

References/links: see linked_artifacts above.
